profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC13 data center at 21830 Uunet Way, Ashburn, Virginia, another node in Equinix's Loudoun County cluster inside Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC13 facility page lists this as a one story, reinforced concrete building of 75,003 square feet (6,968 square meters), smaller and differently constructed than several of Equinix's newer multi-story Ashburn buildings. The page publishes N+1 UPS redundancy and generator redundancy listed as 2/N+1, with generators rated for 30 hours or more of runtime at full load, 120v/208v power distribution, and a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, lower than the 5kVA density Equinix publishes for some of its newer Ashburn buildings. Cooling redundancy is listed as N+20%, floor load capacity as 250 pounds per square foot on a raised floor, and fire suppression as single interlock pre-action, a simpler configuration than the double interlock pre-action systems Equinix lists for some newer buildings nearby. DC13's page also lists a seismic design rating of D under the 2006 Universal Building Code and states the building sits above the 500 year base flood elevation, details not published on every Equinix Ashburn page. Access control is listed as proximity card entrance with mantraps and 24/7 surveillance, and Equinix lists nine certifications for DC13, HECVAT, HIPAA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II, plus a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC13 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project attracted into Loudoun County helped seed the interconnected cluster that followed, including Virginia's early MAE East internet exchange. Equinix opened its first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Data Center Dynamics describes the resulting corridor as roughly 10 million square feet of built data center space region wide, consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power across all operators combined, not Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group, and at least one building number appearing in public address records for the area, DC17, has no active linked page on Equinix's own site at present. Equinix markets its Ashburn buildings collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, along with Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products, without singling out DC13's own peering density or customer roster.

reading.body:
Equinix DC13 is a 75,003 square foot single-story building at 21830 Uunet Way in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's 15-facility cluster in Loudoun County known as Data Center Alley. The building publishes N+1 UPS redundancy, 2/N+1 generator redundancy rated for 30 hours runtime, and N+20% cooling redundancy, but Equinix does not publish an IT load or total power capacity in megawatts for DC13 itself. The facility's 4 kVA minimum cabinet density is lower than Equinix's newer Ashburn buildings, and its single interlock pre-action fire suppression is simpler than double interlock systems Equinix lists for nearby newer facilities.

DC13 holds nine certifications spanning HIPAA, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, ISO 27001, ISO 22301, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and others, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, federal, financial, and critical infrastructure sectors. The building sits above the 500-year base flood elevation and carries a seismic design rating of D under the 2006 Universal Building Code.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley is roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power across all operators combined, anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and seeded by early fiber and peering infrastructure. Equinix's Ashburn campus, anchored by its DC1 and DC2 buildings from the late 1990s, provides access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. DC13 does not publish the megawatt capacity that would place it individually in Virginia's state ranking; among Virginia's 330 mapped data centers, only 25 publish power figures totaling 1,603 megawatts statewide.
